traps: no build file at all: the code is one source-tree unit with name and manifest null
every file ends in .sql; the dialect is in the content: Linguist's heuristics give PLpgSQL for LANGUAGE plpgsql, PLSQL for AUTHID DEFINER and .nextval, TSQL for a GO line and [dbo]
db/sqlserver/vw_open_orders.sql is T-SQL (TOP (100), the N'open' literal, dbo. schema) but matches none of Linguist's T-SQL patterns, so Linguist says SQL: the truth here is TSQL

db/postgres/001_create_orders.sql is plain DDL in the PostgreSQL dialect (BIGSERIAL, TIMESTAMPTZ, JSONB); Linguist has no PostgreSQL language and says SQL, which is right; wrapping it in BEGIN; ... COMMIT; would flip Linguist to PLpgSQL
Linguist classifies SQL as data and the three procedural dialects as programming: a language bar that keeps only programming languages hides the plain DDL
Oracle files use / lines as statement terminators for SQL*Plus; T-SQL uses GO, which is a client batch separator, not SQL
the three folders target three different database servers: no migration tool configuration
